mutations.because: The floor itself. Removing it restores the shared pool alone, which is spent in order and leaves the appended slot — last allocated and most constrained, since it must clear every occupant — with whatever the replay of the operator's existing slots did not use. Because the exhaustive fallback is deliberately closed once a slot has been added, that starvation is reported as `Variation plan shortfall`, i.e. as though the brief could not fit, when the space demonstrably holds the point. Measured over a 4-20 count by 12-seed by 2-distance sweep: 42 briefs whose dense plan succeeds refuse on a single add, and 27 of those place given more turns at the new slot. The test this runs is the one that observes a placement the pool alone cannot reach AND checks the seven occupants stay byte-identical, so it fails if the floor is removed and also if the floor were bought by re-choosing the existing creatives.
command: eighth creative the space has room for

mutations.because: The SCOPE of the floor, which is the half a reader is most likely to think is an unnecessary restriction. Dropping `cursor >= policy.count` extends the floor to every slot, including the dense replay. That is not merely broader: a dense brief whose random draw falls short today drops through to `exhaustiveAccept`, and several plans depend on that fallback being the thing that answers. Give the dense replay extra turns and the random draw reaches a set the fallback used to serve — a DIFFERENT set, silently, for a brief nobody added a slot to. The test that reds is the delete-keeps-its-survivors pair built on exactly such a brief.

note: Two mutations because the change has two claims and they fail differently. #0 is that the floor exists (without it a placeable append is refused). #1 is that the floor stops at `count` (without that bound, dense briefs quietly change plan because the random draw starts reaching sets the exhaustive fallback used to produce). A floor with no bound passes #0 and fails #1, which is the shape of the first draft of this change.
